info.bio:
Wilco es un grupo de rock estadounidense, conocido sobre todo por sus raíces en la música country.
Jeff Tweedy, el principal compositor y cantante de la banda, fue miembro del grupo seminal de los años 1980 y 1990 Uncle Tupelo. Tweedy compartía la tarea de componer y cantar con su compañero de grupo Jay Farrar, que dejó Uncle Tupelo y formó Son Volt. Tweedy formó Wilco con los restantes miembros de Tupelo (el bajista John Stirratt, el batería Ken Coomer y violinista Max Johnston.

scenes.name: Alt-country
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La revolución iniciada en Chicago por Souled American y Uncle Tupelo (No Depression: baladas country con la furia del hardcore) se convierte en los noventa en un género propio: sus herederos abandonan el hardcore por los sonidos más espartanos y tradicionales. Son Volt de Jay Farrar y Wilco de Jeff Tweedy (Being There, Yankee Hotel Foxtrot); Will Oldham (Palace) arranca el movimiento; Freakwater, Ida, Handsome Family, Retsin, Blue Mountain, Whiskeytown, Grant Lee Buffalo, Citizens' Utilities, Willard Grant Conspiracy. El «chamber folk» de Lambchop, Lullaby For The Working Class, Geraldine Fibbers y Pinetop Seven; el country-rock de Volebeats, Ass Ponys, Sixteen Horsepower, Old 97's y los terroristas Grifters; el folk-rock de Swell, Counting Crows, Cracker, Cake, Hootie & The Blowfish; los Black Crowes; Belle And Sebastian, Arab Strap y los polacos Atman.

podcast.title: Early Tiny Desk Appearance - Indie Scene Focus
podcast.body: Wilco was among the bands featured on Tiny Desk when the platform was in its early stages, concentrating almost exclusively on the indie music scene. "En sus inicios, Ténidé es que se centraba casi exclusivamente en la escena Indy, por ahí pasaban bandas como el ancho o builco."

podcast.title: Hipster Music Association
podcast.body: This band was popular among those identifying with hipster culture in the 2010s, aligning with tastes for older or retro sounds. "If that was your scene, I'm going to bet that you and your like-minded friends could also agree on indie era radiohead, LCD sound system, bright eyes, arcade fire, willko, tame and pala, body bear, fleet foxes, and these guys, who were so intertwined with hipster culture, that they actually became a meme."

podcast.title: Independent Label Operations
podcast.body: Wilco manages their own independent record company, DBPM Records, which released their cover of "Record Labels" in 2011. While operating independently, they receive marketing help from Anti-Records, which facilitates distribution through Republic Records, a Universal Music Group sublabel. "DBPM Records, which is another indie company run by Wilco themselves."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Migraines and Painkiller Addiction
podcast.body: Jeff Tweedy has suffered from debilitating migraines since childhood, which led to an addiction to Vicodin, Oxycontin, and later stolen morphine. His Vicodin use began in the late 90s, where painkillers became necessary for him to feel normal and also suppressed his panic attacks. "Jeff's condition, which has been with him since he was a kid, led to an addiction to Vicodin and Oxycontin and eventually stolen morphine. The Vicodin started in the late 90s and eventually he only felt normal when he was on painkillers. It also kind of helped that they suppressed his panic attacks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rehab and Recovery
podcast.body: Jeff Tweedy eventually sought rehab to address both his crippling migraines and his addiction to painkillers. While panic attacks still occur, he is now in a much better place overall, with his recovery evident in subsequent musical works. "The good news is that Jeff finally sought rehab for both problems, the migraines and the painkiller addiction. The panic attack still come but overall he's in a lot better place."

xref.title: Another Roadside Attraction Festival (1993)
xref.body: The Tragically Hip organized the festival "Another Roadside Attraction" in 1993, 1995, and 1997. This festival was one of several Canadian-based summer music events during the 90s, showcasing the growing strength and popularity of domestic music. "There was another roadside attraction, which was organized by the Trajically Hip in 1993, 1995 and 1997."

xref.title: Catholic Upbringing and Fear
xref.body: Gerard Way grew up in a very Catholic family, which instilled in him a significant "fear of God." This upbringing made him so scared that he was afraid to walk past the funeral home located near his house, and he described Sunday school as being akin to a Vincent Price movie. "Gerard Wei of Mike and Wilco Romance grew up in a very, very Catholic family. He had so much of the fear of God injected into him that he was too scared to walk by the funeral home down from his house. He says that Sunday school was like a Vincent Price movie."

xref.title: Extensive Musician Dating History
xref.body: Winona Ryder, an actress, has been connected to or dated a significant number of musicians, totaling 22 individuals according to a count from the transcript. Her relationships included Dave Grohl, Ryan Adams, Pete Yorn, Jack White, Julian from The Strokes, Conor Oberst of Bright Eyes, possibly Jeff Tweedy from Wilco, Irish musician Damien Rice, Tre Cool of Green Day, Marky Walberg (Marky Mark), Stephen Jenkins of Third Eye Blind, Everlast (whose real name is Eric Shorty), John Kay from Jamiroquai, Adam Duritz of Counting Crows (who also dated Jennifer Aniston and Courtney Cox), Chris Isaak, Dave Pirner of Soul Asylum, Paul Westerberg of The Replacements (which was noted as potentially during her "Minneapolis punk period"), Mike Nesmith of The Monkees, Johnny Depp, and Evan Dando of The Lemonheads. The last heard connection was an engagement to Blake Sennett, who plays guitar in Rilo Kiley. "I count 22 musicians."
